claim: Portuguese commercial and religious expansion in sixteenth- and seventeenth-century Sri Lanka displaced Muslim merchant communities from a number of coastal settlements and weakened their access to maritime trade; part of the affected population and commercial activity shifted toward the Kandyan interior and the eastern littoral.
bounded_by: Displacement was neither instantaneous nor total, and Muslim commercial networks persisted or reconfigured through South Indian and inland connections. Specific town-by-town expulsions require Portuguese/Dutch documentary anchors.
notes: Bridge candidate: European competition for maritime trade -> spatial redistribution of Muslim communities -> stronger functional links with Kandy and the east coast.
